original_question: Let N ≥ 1. There exists a constant γN > 0 such that for all dominant rational maps f : PN 99K PN we have deg(f n+1 ) δ(f ) ≥ γN · min . 0≤n<N deg(f n ).
target_in_paper: Section 14, Conjecture 14.14. This is the uniform lower-bound conjecture for the dynamical degree of a dominant rational self-map of projective space, introduced immediately after Conjecture 14.13 as a way to imply that family-degeneration statement.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main shape of the statement: fix N ≥ 1; there should be a positive constant γ_N depending only on N; the quantifier is over all dominant rational self-maps f of P^N; and the inequality compares the dynamical degree δ(f) with data from the degrees of early iterates of f.
missing_details: The key quantity is a minimum of ratios deg(f^{n+1})/deg(f^n); the draft’s formula drops this quotient structure, which is the core of the conjecture.
The index range is exactly 0 ≤ n < N, i.e. n = 0, 1, ..., N−1.
Because the minimum starts at n = 0, one must specify f^0 = id_{P^N}, so deg(f^0) = 1.
The dynamical degree must be defined: δ(f) = lim_{m→∞} (deg(f^m))^{1/m}.
The ambient field K is implicit in the section setup: f is represented by homogeneous polynomials f_0, ..., f_N in K[X_0, ..., X_N] of a common degree.
The degree of a rational map is the common degree after removing any common factors among the homogeneous coordinate polynomials; the same convention applies to the iterates f^m.
The map is only assumed dominant and rational; the conjecture does not assume that f is a morphism, birational, polynomial, or algebraically stable.
The paper adds an explicit note that γ_N is not allowed to depend on the particular map f, only on N.
refined_question: Fix an integer N ≥ 1. Does there exist a constant γ_N > 0, depending only on N, such that for every field K and every dominant rational self-map f of P^N defined over K, with dynamical degree δ(f) := lim_{m→∞} (deg(f^m))^{1/m} and with f^0 the identity map, one has δ(f) ≥ γ_N · min_{0≤n<N} (deg(f^{n+1})/deg(f^n))?
justification: The draft is aiming at Conjecture 14.14, not the neighboring family statement Conjecture 14.13 or the later growth question Question 14.16. The match is decisive because Conjecture 14.14 is the unique statement in the paper asserting the existence of constants γ_N > 0 with a lower bound for δ(f) in terms of the first N degree ratios of iterates. The nearby context in Section 14 defines rational self-maps of P^N, defines δ(f), recalls algebraic stability, explains that Conjecture 14.14 would imply Conjecture 14.13, and records Xie’s theorem proving the N = 2 case.
